correctness.rationale: C PASS: Inspected the actual stationary two-sided diffusion with positive Q_t=1/8−(rU_t+delta E_t)^2/2. U_t=delta∫_{−∞}^t e^(−a(t−s))E_s ds has |rU+delta E|<=delta/a<1/2, so Q>0 and stochastic integrals exist. Generator L on UE,U²,U³E,U⁴ yields stated exact moments; the centered pair (U²−EU²,UE−EUE) has triangular drift M and covariance S. For r>0, v=(r²,2r delta) has positive components; S and e^(M^Tt) are entrywise positive, proving C_Q(t)>0. Laplace resolvent L(z)=v^TS(zI−M^T)^−1v/4 gives Var(V_k)=L(k)/k, Cov(V_k,V_l)=[L(k)+L(l)]/(k+l), and conditional Gaussian identities give cum4=3L(k)/k and positive cross-squares covariance. Algebra simplifies to the printed rational cumulant; its denominator and residual polynomial are strictly positive on 1/2<a<=1 and c>0, and factor (a−1)^2 enforces the iff r=0 boundary. At r=0 Q constant, so the Brownian-driven modes really are independent Gaussians; their unconditional zero covariance for r>0 does not imply independence. Independently derived the same symbolic cumulant from both resolvent and stationary mixed U,V moment recursion, using SymPy identity simplification, not source code.

value.rationale: V PASS: Detecting strictly non-Gaussian stationary marginals and dependence between two uncorrelated fluctuation modes in a natural, already-studied critical switching model directly answers a structural probabilistic question that second moments cannot resolve. The exact iff boundary and positive dependence are independently useful.

final_claim: For the stationary telegraph-modulated two-mode OU fluctuation diffusion with a=1-r>1/2, r=rho+kappa>=0, delta>0, c>0, r+2delta<1, the exact fourth cumulant is the displayed rational expression in RESULT.md, positive iff r>0. Its Gaussian conditional modes are uncorrelated; they are unconditionally independent iff r=0, otherwise their squared amplitudes have strictly positive covariance.
limitations: There is a genuine b parameter b=1−rho+kappa; resulting damping ell=2b−1 must stay positive. Modes are only conditionally independent for r>0.
